subject: POC: Prompt set & eval dataset collection — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-16T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: POC: Prompt set & eval dataset collection — next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the POC scope and what we need from your side to get started.

Recap (short):
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood inference runtime on your clinical triage assistant prompts and determine latency/cost/quality tradeoffs for a 1-month pilot.
- Success criteria (your ask):
  - >= 95% accuracy vs. your gold labels on the top-1 intent agreement (across sampled prompts)
  - Median generation latency < 450ms for 512-token requests on our dedicated pool
  - Cost target: <= $0.0025/token for production-like traffic profile

POC evaluation plan (proposed):
1) Data collection (you): sample prompts + representative logs (see details below) — deliver by Tue 7/21
2) Ingest & baseline run (Redwood SRE/SE): 7/22–7/24 (Aditya will onboard model/config)
3) Eval & tuning (joint): 7/25–7/30 — run prompt set, measure metrics, iterate on temperature/decoding/quantization
4) Final review & go/no-go: 7/31 — short sync and shared report

Ownership:
- Acme Health: Alex (product) + Sara (data engineer) — provide prompts, gold labels, access to logs
- Redwood: Marissa (AE) owner of success criteria & schedule; Aditya (SE) owner of ingestion & baseline runs

What we need from you (data checklist):
- A sample prompt set (10–50 examples) spanning happy & edge cases (CSV or JSONL). Include columns: prompt_text, expected_label, context_metadata (optional).
- 1 week of anonymized request/response logs (redact PHI) or a representative subset. If you can’t share logs, provide synthetic traffic profile (qps, avg tokens per request).
- Any scoring script or rubric you use for intent matching (if available).

Attachments & links: I’ve attached a small sample template (poc_eval_template.xlsx) and an example CSV (sample_prompts.csv). Please upload your full dataset to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPOC-AcmeHealth — mark files with prefix ACME_POC_ so we can track.

Quick asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm by end of day tomorrow that you’ll be able to deliver the sample prompts and logs by Tue 7/21?
- If yes, we’ll schedule the technical kickoff with Aditya for 7/22 10:00am PT (30 min).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Alex / Marissa —

Thanks — quick technical checklist to make ingestion smooth:
- Preferred formats: JSONL (one JSON per line) or CSV with UTF-8 encoding. For JSONL please include keys: request_id, prompt_text, expected_label (optional), metadata (optional).
- Max file size per upload: 2GB — if larger, split into shards named ACME_POC_01.jsonl etc.
- Anonymization: remove direct PHI fields (names, MRNs); if you must include tokens that look like PHI, replace with <REDACTED>.
- Tokenization note: we’ll run our tokenizer during baseline — please send prompts in raw text, not already tokenized.
- If you have scoring scripts, upload as a .py or .ipynb (we can run in a sandbox).

I attached a short ingestion spec and a sample JSONL snippet for reference. If you can follow the sample schema, our ingestion will be plug-and-play.

Also: for the latency target, please include a representative request-size distribution (p50/p95 token counts) so we can size the dedicated pool appropriately.

See attached: prompt_ingest_spec.md and example snippet.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
